requirements.statement: In both the animals frontend and the INS frontend, a signed-in trader's service navigation offers, in order: Dashboard, Templates, Address book, Manage account and Log out, with the current item marked active (Templates on every template page, Address book on every address-book page).
requirements.why: DR2.1 adds Templates to the navigation; Log out stays because a real signed-in trader must be able to sign out, which the prototype has no sign-in to show.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both frontends show Dashboard, Address book, Manage account and Log out, with no Templates item (repo-frontend-p1-008, repo-insfrontend-p4-006).

requirements.statement: Every page shows the Alpha phase banner 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.', whose feedback link is an email to APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk.
requirements.why: DR2.1 shows the banner on every page; DR1 ruled the feedback destination because the prototype's link is a placeholder.
requirements.deltaNote: Both frontends already show this banner with the APHA service desk mailto (repo-frontend-p1-017, repo-insfrontend-p4-017).

requirements.statement: The Manage account navigation item stays a placeholder that links nowhere ('#') and is never shown as active.
requirements.why: DR2.1 gives Manage account no destination and no source names one.
requirements.deltaNote: Both frontends already link Manage account to '#' (repo-frontend-p1-013, repo-insfrontend-p4-009).

requirements.statement: The Commodity details page is captioned 'Description of the goods'; every other journey page keeps the caption it has today, which already matches DR2.1.
requirements.why: DR2.1 places Commodity details under '2. Description of the goods' and captions the page to match.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Commodity details page is captioned 'About the consignment' with the origin, commodity, identification and reason pages (repo-frontend-p1-139).

requirements.statement: A journey page's Back link goes to the overview when the page was opened from the overview, to the template when it was opened from a template, and otherwise to the page before it in the journey (for example the main import reason page back to 'What are you importing?', and Commodity details back to 'What are you importing?').
requirements.why: DR2.1 sets one back-link rule for the linear journey; the real pages send every Back link to the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the commodity search, Commodity details and import reason pages always link Back to the overview (repo-frontend-p5-034, repo-frontend-p5-049, repo-frontend-p7-002).

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' takes a new notification through the journey in this order: origin, what are you importing, main import reason, commodity details, identification details (when a commodity needs identifiers), additional details, arrival details, transit countries (rail or road only), transporter, upload documents, consignment addresses, contact address, review, declaration. The CPH number and permanent address pages are reached from the consignment addresses page, not as steps of their own.
requirements.why: DR2.1 asks the main reason for import before the commodity details and treats the CPH as part of the consignment addresses.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the opening run asks commodity details before the import reason and runs on from the addresses page to the CPH number page as its own step (repo-frontend-p1-110).

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the consignment addresses page goes to the contact address page, or to the overview when every overview section is already complete.
requirements.why: DR2.1 continues the linear journey from the addresses page rather than dropping the trader on the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: Today submitting the addresses page saves nothing and goes to the overview (repo-frontend-p9-026).

requirements.statement: Pages the overview links to end with 'Save and continue', a secondary 'Save and return to overview' and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link; pages reached from another page (party pickers, CPH number, transporter type and add pages, permanent address) end with 'Save and continue' alone; no control says 'hub' or 'Cancel and return to dashboard'.
requirements.why: DR1 ruled the page endings (rule (b)) and the 'overview' wording on these same differences, and DR1 judgements outrank the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals frontend already ends pages this way and never says 'hub' (repo-frontend-p1-072, repo-frontend-p1-073, repo-frontend-p1-076); new pages this programme adds follow the same rule.

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, each journey page ends with a primary 'Save and return' (to the review page), a secondary 'Save and continue' and a link-styled 'Save and return to overview', with no cancel link.
requirements.why: DR2.1 keeps an amending trader close to the review they are re-submitting from.

requirements.statement: The status strip above a notification page shows the status tag and the reference; while amending, the tag reads 'Amend' and a link-styled 'Cancel amend' button beside it opens the cancel-amendment dialog.
requirements.why: DR2.1 names the amending state 'Amend' and lets the trader cancel the amendment from any page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the strip shows a yellow 'Amending' tag and offers no cancel-amend control (repo-frontend-p1-029).

requirements.statement: Cancelling an amendment is confirmed in a modal dialog headed 'Are you sure you want to cancel this amendment?' with 'Yes, cancel amendment', a 'Go back' link-styled button and a Close button; closing it changes nothing, and the existing cancel-amendment page stays as the route without JavaScript.
requirements.why: DR2.1 confirms cancelling in a dialog on the page the trader is on; the page route keeps the action working without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: Today cancelling an amendment is a separate page headed 'Cancel this amendment?' with 'Yes, cancel amendment' and 'No, return to notification' (repo-frontend-p3-080, repo-frontend-p3-083).

requirements.statement: A submitted notification is amended from its review page: 'Amend this notification' opens a dialog headed 'Amend notification' asking 'Are you sure you want to change this notification?' with 'Yes, continue' and 'No, go back'; confirming puts the notification into amendment and opens its review page.
requirements.why: DR2.1 starts amending from the notification itself with a confirmation, and lands the trader on the review page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Amend is a dashboard card button that puts the notification into amendment and opens its overview, with no confirmation (repo-frontend-p3-049, repo-frontend-p3-061).

requirements.statement: When an amended notification's answers differ from the submitted version, the review page is headed 'Review before re-submitting'; changes to anything that is not an answer do not count.
requirements.why: DR2.1 tells the trader they are about to re-submit a changed notification.

requirements.statement: While amending, the review page shows a secondary 'Cancel amend' button beside Continue, which opens the cancel-amendment dialog.
requirements.why: DR2.1 lets the trader abandon the amendment from the review page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review page shows a 'Cancel amendment' link to the cancel-amend page (repo-frontend-p13-110).

requirements.statement: Only live animals is built: 'Create new' starts a live-animals notification straight on its origin page, with no notification type page.
requirements.why: The goal names the live-animals journey, and only live animals has a real journey; the type page would offer types no real service builds.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Start a new notification' on the INS dashboard goes to the animals dashboard, and starting there opens the origin page (repo-insfrontend-p1-029, repo-frontend-p3-007).

requirements.statement: The germinal-products journey (its commodity list, total gross weight, number of packages, storage temperature, its reduced reason and purpose lists and its dashboard section) is not built.
requirements.why: Out of scope by default: the goal names the live-animals journey, and germinal products would be a new journey rather than a change to a real one.

requirements.statement: The dashboard home's plants section and the inspection pages ('Inspection required', 'Consignments due at the border control post (BCP)') are not built.
requirements.why: Out of scope by default: plants is another service's journey, and DR2.1 shows inspection only for plants, from data no real service records.

requirements.statement: Prototype scaffolding is not built: the service index page with its release cards, the version mount and session nests, the /prototype/reason-for-import shortcut, demo states assigned by list position, and the seeded demo notifications, templates, addresses and transporters.
requirements.why: Out of scope: these exist to run the prototype, not as service behaviour.

requirements.statement: The DR2.1 dashboard (home, Live animals list and drill-downs) and the DR2.1 address book are built in the INS frontend, reached from the Dashboard and Address book navigation items of both frontends.
requirements.why: DR1 ruled that the dashboard and the address book live in the INS frontend, and that ruling outranks the single-app prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS frontend serves a reference-search table dashboard and an untyped address book (repo-insfrontend-p1-001, repo-insfrontend-p2-001), and the animals frontend keeps its own dashboard.

requirements.statement: The live-animals journey's dashboard links (the Dashboard navigation item, the overview's 'Return to dashboard', the confirmation page's 'Return to your dashboard' and the landing after a delete) go to the INS dashboard; the animals frontend's own /live-animals dashboard stays unchanged until a ruling retires it.
requirements.why: DR2.1 has one dashboard; this keeps the trader on it while the real service runs two.
requirements.deltaNote: Today those links go to the animals frontend's dashboard at /live-animals (repo-frontend-p1-010, repo-frontend-p4-052, repo-frontend-p14-050).

requirements.statement: The dashboard home has the caption 'Dashboard' above the heading 'Import notification service', a primary 'Create new' button, a secondary 'Use template' button to Manage templates, and a 'Live animals' section with a 'View dashboard' link and two glance cards: 'Action needed' ('Tasks requiring your attention', a count, 'View tasks') and 'Status updates' ('Changes in the past 24 hours', a count, 'View updates'). Counts are counted from the trader's notifications.
requirements.why: DR2.1 makes the dashboard a signed-in landing page that sends the trader to what needs attention; real counts replace the prototype's fixed numbers.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS dashboard is headed 'Dashboard' with no caption, and shows only a reference search and a table of notifications (repo-insfrontend-p1-003, repo-insfrontend-p1-004).

requirements.statement: The Live animals list page has the caption 'Dashboard', the heading 'Live animals', a Back link to the home, 'Create new' and 'Use template' buttons, a 'Summary' of the two glance cards counted live for live animals, and a 'Notifications' section.
requirements.why: DR2.1 gives each notification category its own dashboard page.

requirements.statement: The notification list has one search field labelled 'Search by' with the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor' and a magnifying-glass Search button; a search matches any of those, and the searched text stays in the field.
requirements.why: DR2.1 lets a trader find a notification by what they remember about it, not only its exact reference.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS search is 'Search by notification reference' and ins-backend matches only a complete reference exactly (repo-insfrontend-p1-007, repo-insbackend-p1-059).

requirements.statement: The notification list has a 'Sort by:' select offering 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', which orders the list; the list is always sorted, Newest first by default, with no 'Select one' option.
requirements.why: DR2.1's sort labels, with DR1's ruling that the dashboard is always sorted.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS sort offers four arrival and last-updated options applied by an 'Update sort' button (repo-insfrontend-p1-019, repo-insfrontend-p1-024).

requirements.statement: The notification list has a collapsible 'Additional filters' section, open when any filter is set, with 'By arrival date' radios (Today, Tomorrow, Next 7 days), 'By date range' start and end date pickers hinted 'For example, 27/3/2026', and a 'Status' select (Select one, Action required, Submitted, Completed); the chosen filters narrow the list.
requirements.why: DR2.1 lets a trader narrow the list by arrival and status; a real service must apply what the prototype only displays.

requirements.statement: The notification list has three tabs, 'In progress (N)', 'Draft' and 'Completed', each with a subheading ('Notifications in progress', 'Draft notifications', 'Completed notifications'); In progress lists submitted and action-required notifications, Draft lists drafts and Completed lists completed ones.
requirements.why: DR2.1 separates work in flight from drafts and finished notifications.

requirements.statement: Notification lists show 8 notifications a page with numbered GOV.UK pagination and Previous and Next links; page links keep the tab and sort.
requirements.why: DR2.1 pages its lists in eights.
requirements.deltaNote: Today ins-backend serves 25 notifications a page (repo-insbackend-p1-034).

requirements.statement: Each notification shows as a card labelled for screen readers 'Notification <reference>', with the reference as its heading and two rows: Commodity, Arrival date (dd/mm/yyyy), Consignee and Notification status; then Number of animals, Origin and Consignor. A submitted notification's status reads 'Submitted' as plain text, a draft shows a 'Draft' tag.
requirements.why: DR2.1 identifies a consignment by what, from where, when and between whom, replacing the reference-and-status table.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS dashboard is a table of reference, raw status code, origin country, commodity and arrival date (repo-insfrontend-p1-037, repo-insfrontend-p1-040).

requirements.statement: A notification card's actions depend on its status: a draft offers Resume, Copy as new and Delete; a submitted notification offers View, Amend, Copy as new and Delete; one being amended offers Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment and Delete.
requirements.why: DR1 rejected flattening the card to Copy as new and View; the default carries that judgement to the INS dashboard.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS dashboard rows have a single View link (repo-insfrontend-p1-047); the status-driven actions exist only on the animals-frontend dashboard.

requirements.statement: A notification needing action shows on its card in the error style with a red marker, an 'Action required' tag and its message: 'ITAHC is missing' when no ITAHC document is attached, otherwise 'Information is missing' when required animal identifiers are incomplete.
requirements.why: DR2.1 flags submitted notifications that still owe something before import.

requirements.statement: An 'Action needed' page (caption 'Action needed', heading 'Tasks requiring your attention', description 'Add missing information or upload documents to prevent your consignment from being delayed.') lists the notifications needing action for its category, with the same search and sort, a 'Show <first>-<last> of <total> results' count, 8 a page, and a Back link to the category list.
requirements.why: DR2.1's 'View tasks' drill-down gathers what the trader must fix.

requirements.statement: The Completed tab, the Status updates card and its 'Changes in past 24 hours' page are built but stay empty (count 0) until a service records completion or status changes; Delayed states, the inspection card and page, and the Messages link are not built.
requirements.why: DR2.1 shows states that come from border processes no real service records yet.

requirements.statement: After a delete, the dashboard shows a green 'Success' banner reading '<reference> has been deleted' (or 'Notification has been deleted' when the reference is unknown), shown once and dismissing itself after 5 seconds.
requirements.why: DR2.1 confirms the delete on the list the trader returns to.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a delete lands on the animals dashboard with a 'Notification deleted' banner reading 'The notification has been deleted.' (repo-frontend-p3-062).

requirements.statement: Every dashboard list, tab, count and search shows only the signed-in organisation's notifications.
requirements.why: DR2.1's dashboards show the trader's own work; showing every trader's notifications is an access-control gap.
requirements.deltaNote: Today ins-backend serves every non-deleted notification from every organisation to every caller (repo-insbackend-p1-068, repo-insfrontend-p4-126).

requirements.statement: The INS read model holds what the DR2.1 dashboard shows and filters on: consignee and consignor names, number of animals, commodity common name, arrival date, status (including action required and its message) and the notification's organisation, filled from the animals backend's events.
requirements.why: The dashboard cannot show, search or filter on fields the read model does not carry.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the read model holds only reference, status, origin country, commodity, arrival date and last updated (repo-insbackend-p1-002).

requirements.statement: On submission the animals backend works out the items still outstanding (no ITAHC document; required animal identifiers incomplete) and records the notification as submitted with action required when any are outstanding, publishing that with its other events.
requirements.why: DR2.1 derives 'Submitted action required' from what the notification still owes; no real status carries it today.

requirements.statement: A 'Manage templates' page (heading and title 'Manage templates', description 'Select, manage or create new notification templates', a 'Create new template' button) lists the organisation's templates under 'My templates' with a 'Show 1-N of N results' count and a 'Sort by:' select; each card is labelled 'Template <title>', shows its category and title with 'View template' and 'Use template' links, and lists Commodity, Origin, Consignee and Consignor.
requirements.why: DR2.1 adds templates so a trader can start repeat consignments without re-entering them.

requirements.statement: 'Create new template' asks 'Enter template name' (caption 'Create a new template'; a blank name saves as 'Untitled template') and then runs the journey from the origin page in template mode: the overview shows a 'Template' tag and the template name, headed 'Template tasklist', with no Documents section, 'Review template' and 'Return to manage templates'; the arrival date, documents and declaration are not asked; the review is headed 'Review your template' and ends with 'Save template', which returns to Manage templates with the banner '<name> saved to templates'.
requirements.why: DR2.1 builds a template through the same pages as a notification, leaving out what changes every time.

requirements.statement: A template keeps the answers DR2.1 saves (origin, commodity and species, numbers, identifiers, reason and purpose, certified for, unweaned, port of entry, transport, transporter, place of origin, CPH and contact address) and never an arrival date or documents.
requirements.why: DR2.1 fixes what a template carries so a notification started from one needs only the consignment-specific answers.

requirements.statement: A template's page (caption 'Templates', the title as heading, 'Date created:', 'Use template' and a red 'Delete' button, Back to Manage templates) shows its answers in the review's cards; each card's Change link edits that section in template mode and returns to the template with '<title> has been updated'.
requirements.why: DR2.1 lets a trader check and correct a template in place.

requirements.statement: 'Use template' starts a new draft notification with a new reference, seeded from the template (consignment parties from its addresses, contact address from its contact or place of origin), and opens its overview.
requirements.why: DR2.1 turns a template into a notification in one step.

requirements.statement: Deleting a template, or discarding one being created, asks 'Delete this template?' with a 'Name' row, 'Confirm that you want to delete this template.' and 'This action cannot be undone.', a red 'Yes, delete' and a 'No, cancel' link; confirming returns to Manage templates with '<title> has been deleted'.
requirements.why: DR2.1 confirms template deletion the same way as notification and address deletion.

requirements.statement: A saved address carries one or more uses (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination, Branch address), grouped into the categories Origin and Consignor, Destination, Consignee and Importer, and Branch; the address-book API accepts, stores, returns and filters by them.
requirements.why: DR2.1 and DR1 both type saved addresses so each picker offers only the addresses that fit the role.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an address-book record has no type or use and the API rejects a request carrying one (repo-addressbook-p1-096, repo-addressbook-p3-046).

requirements.statement: The address book list is headed 'Address book' with the intro 'Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications', an 'Add a new address' button, a collapsible 'Filter addresses' panel (Search, placeholder 'Search by name, address or country'; a Type select listing the tab's uses), four category tabs (Origin and Consignor; Destination, Consignee and Importer; Transporter; Branch) each with its own heading, a 'Showing <start>-<end> of <total>' line, a table of Name, Type, Address (one line per address line) and Country with a 'View' link per row (Transporter tab: Name, Address, Approval number, Type), 8 addresses a page and a one-time success banner.
requirements.why: DR2.1 organises the address book by what each address is for.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list's intro reads 'Manage addresses used across import and export services.', it has one search box, no tabs or types, Name, Address and Country columns and 25 a page (repo-insfrontend-p2-004, repo-insfrontend-p2-016).

requirements.statement: An address-book search matches, case-insensitively and anywhere in the text, an address's name, use labels, address lines and country, and a transporter's approval number.
requirements.why: DR2.1's search covers everything the list shows.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address-book q search matches only name, town or city and postcode (repo-addressbook-p3-032, repo-addressbook-p3-033).

requirements.statement: An address's page is headed with its name and lists Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional) and County (optional) only when filled, Town or city, Postcode or Zip code, Country, Email address and Phone number, with a secondary 'Edit' and a warning 'Delete' button and a Back link to where the trader came from.
requirements.why: DR2.1 shows only the facts an address has.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page always lists all nine rows, blanks included, and labels county 'County' (repo-insfrontend-p2-040, repo-insfrontend-p2-049).

requirements.statement: Editing an address is headed 'Edit address and contact details', groups the fields under 'Address' and 'Contact details', keeps the address's uses, ends with 'Save changes' and a secondary 'Cancel' (back to the address's page), and after saving returns to the list with '<Name> address updated'.
requirements.why: DR2.1's edit page and confirmation.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the edit page is headed 'Edit address details' with no section headings, Cancel goes to the list, and the banner reads '{name} updated in your address book' (repo-insfrontend-p3-083, repo-insfrontend-p3-090, repo-insfrontend-p3-092).

requirements.statement: Every address form uses DR2.1's required-field messages: 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Select a country', 'Enter an email address' and 'Enter a phone number', in the INS frontend and the address-book API.
requirements.why: DR2.1 words the same rules differently from today's address book.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the messages read 'Enter a name', 'Enter a postcode', 'Enter a country' and 'Enter a telephone number' (repo-insfrontend-p3-044, repo-addressbook-p1-010, repo-addressbook-p1-028).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address asks 'Delete this address?' with an 'Address' row (name, lines and country), 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.' and 'This action cannot be undone.', a warning 'Yes, delete' button and a 'No, cancel' link; afterwards the list shows '<Name> address deleted'.
requirements.why: DR2.1's delete confirmation, matching its notification and template deletes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page is 'Delete address' asking 'Are you sure you want to delete <name> from your address book?' with 'Yes, delete this address' and a Cancel button (repo-insfrontend-p2-054, repo-insfrontend-p2-055).

requirements.statement: Adding an address starts with 'Choose an address type' (caption 'Add a new address') offering Origin or Consignor ('Place of origin, Consignor'), Destination, Consignee or Importer ('Place of destination, Consignee, Importer'), Transporter ('Private, Commercial') and Branch ('Branch address'); continuing with none chosen shows 'Select an address type'; Transporter goes to the add-transporter pages.
requirements.why: DR2.1 asks what an address is for before collecting it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Add a new address' opens one 'Add address details' form with no type question (repo-insfrontend-p3-003).

requirements.statement: The add-details step is headed 'Add address and contact details' (caption 'Add new address'): Origin or Consignor shows the manual fields with a country select; Destination and Branch offer 'Search for an address' and 'Enter address manually', with the country fixed to United Kingdom; fields sit under 'Address' and 'Contact details'; a uses question (hint 'Select where this address can be used') requires at least one use ('Select what this address can be used for'); 'Save and continue' returns to the list on the new address's category with '<name> address added to your address book', and 'Cancel and return to address book' leaves without saving.
requirements.why: DR2.1 collects origin-side addresses anywhere in the world and destination-side and branch addresses in the UK.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add page is headed 'Add address details' with 'Enter address details' and 'Enter contact details' sections, no search, no uses, and the banner reads '{name} added to your address book' (repo-insfrontend-p3-003, repo-insfrontend-p3-005, repo-insfrontend-p3-077).

requirements.statement: 'Search for an address' (placeholder 'Start typing...') is a type-ahead over real addresses: picking a result fills the name, address lines, town or city, postcode and country, leaving email and phone to the trader; 'Enter address manually' is always offered and is the route without JavaScript.
requirements.why: DR2.1 finds UK addresses by search; a real search needs a real address source.

requirements.statement: The address book only ever shows, changes or deletes the signed-in organisation's addresses.
requirements.why: Organisation scoping is a real authorisation constraint; DR2.1 has no organisations to show it.
requirements.deltaNote: Every address-book call is scoped by the session's organisation in path and header (repo-insfrontend-p3-072, repo-addressbook-p2-094).

requirements.statement: The consignment addresses page (caption 'Consignment parties', heading 'Consignment addresses', intro 'Add all the addresses that are involved in the consignment.', warning 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud' with no full stop) shows each party as a heading with its hint; an unanswered party shows a named link ('Add a place of origin', 'Add a consignor', 'Add a consignee', 'Add an importer', 'Add a place of destination'); an answered party shows its name, address lines and country in an inset with a 'Change' link. The consignor party is named 'Consignor'.
requirements.why: DR2.1 shows each chosen address in full and names each add link.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page is a summary list of names with 'Not added yet' and a shared 'Add' link, no intro, a warning ending in a full stop, and the consignor titled 'Consignor or exporter' (repo-frontend-p9-007, repo-frontend-p9-010, repo-frontend-p9-011, repo-frontend-p9-034).

requirements.statement: Once a place of origin is chosen, the empty consignor row offers 'Same as place of origin'; once a consignee is chosen, the empty importer and place of destination rows each offer 'Same as consignee'. Pressing one copies that address into the row and reloads the page; the copy does not change if the source changes later.
requirements.why: DR2.1 saves the trader picking the same address twice.

requirements.statement: A party picker (caption 'Consignment parties', the party's heading and hint) has a secondary 'Add a new address' button, a search ('Search', hint 'Name, address or country'; the place of origin picker searches by country) that filters the table as the trader types, a 'Select an address' heading with 'Showing <visible> out of <total> results', and every address for the role on one page in a table of a radio ('Select <name>'), Name, Address (one line per line) and Country with a 'View' link to that address's page in the address book.
requirements.why: DR2.1 shows the whole role list on one page and links each row to the saved address.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the picker shows five addresses a page with server pagination, a 'Selected address:' inset, a 'Showing N of T addresses' caption and an in-place 'View details' disclosure (repo-frontend-p9-058, repo-frontend-p9-062, repo-frontend-p9-065).

requirements.statement: Each party picker lists only the addresses whose uses include its role (the consignor picker also accepts consignor-or-exporter and exporter), and an address with several uses appears on every matching picker.
requirements.why: DR2.1 and DR1 filter each picker to its role so a trader is not offered an overseas farm as a place of destination.
requirements.deltaNote: Today all five pickers offer the whole organisation address book whatever the role (document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-019).

requirements.statement: Saving a party picker with no address chosen shows no error and returns to the consignment addresses page, leaving that party as it was.
requirements.why: DR2.1 lets the trader back out of a picker without an error.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving with nothing chosen and no address held re-renders the picker with 'Select ... from the list' and a 400 (repo-frontend-p9-080).

requirements.statement: A picker's 'Add a new address' opens DR2.1's journey add-address page (caption 'Add new address', heading 'Add address and contact details'): origin-side parties enter any country by hand, destination-side parties search UK addresses or enter one by hand; 'What else should this address be used for?' (hint 'This address is being added as a <role> address...') offers the other roles on the same side; 'Save and select' saves to the address book with the role and ticked uses, selects it and returns to the consignment addresses page with '<name> address added to your address book', and 'Save and return to address page' saves it and returns to the picker.
requirements.why: DR2.1 adds and selects a missing address without leaving the journey; the real address book has one writer.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Add a new address' hands over to the INS add page, which looks the same as its address-book add page apart from the cancel label, and returns the new address selected on the picker (repo-frontend-p9-133, repo-frontend-p9-149, repo-insfrontend-p3-107).

requirements.statement: The contact address page is headed 'Contact address for consignment' with no caption, opens with 'This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.', then 'Select an address' and 'If the correct address is not shown, add a new branch address, then return to this page.' (linking to the address-book add); it lists only branch addresses as radios (name as label, address as hint), requires a choice ('Select a contact address'), and selects a branch address added from it on return.
requirements.why: DR2.1 and DR1 limit the contact to the trader's own branch addresses and explain who the contact is.
